subject: Class 379 Electrostar: Great Northern 2025-26 (ex-Greater Anglia white, GN branding) and Greater Anglia/Stansted Express 2019-21 (LE)
method: Bodyside door positions and car length from 1D projective fits along one row through door edges on g018 (379018, 2026) and g003 (379003, 2025); the WestRail642fan diagram (dia) only for layout order. Face measured head-on on the telephoto g024 (379024, 2025-04-04) at 301 px/m (body silhouette 2.80 m at lamp height; head lens 69x68.5 px, so vertical scale = horizontal), cross-checked on l017 (head-on, 291 px/m from the lamp spacing) and g018 (rail-anchored column). Heights anchored at the cap's orange line bottom = 3.26 m (the bodyside cantrail line sweeps into it), checked against the rail on g018. Side = train's RIGHT side (left half of the face as seen head-on) on g018, g003 and l029.

calibration.notes: Face: body silhouette at row 1470 spans 1445.5-2288.5 px = 843 px = 2.80 m; white margins outside the yellow panels 73 px each side (head-on, symmetric). Vertical = horizontal (round headlamp lens 69 x 68.5 px; sleeper foreshortening says ~4 deg depression, a distant telephoto). Rail check: gauge at the first visible sleepers ~314 px/m (a few metres nearer the camera). Side: g018 row 1436-1471 through door edges, projective fit (1D) of [cab door rear 1.787, door1 front/rear, door2 front/rear] residuals -0.6/3.4/-3.0/-0.9/1.2 px. Bodyside heights: g018 col 1450, orange line 1197.5 px = 3.30 m to body bottom 1858 = 0.94 m (279.9 px/m).

trace.cab.length: Published DMC/DMS 20.39 m (Wikipedia 'Bombardier Electrostar' dimensions table, classes 377 and 379 share one row; includes gangway), intermediate 19.99 m (same table, 357/376 rows). Body face to car end 20.20 m as the 377. g018 projective fit through cab door, door 1, door 2 and the car end at 293 px: L=20.0-20.2 fits at rms 1.9-2.3 px; L=20.70 (dia: 606 px/29.3) at rms 5.8 px with the end residual +9 px, and the diagram-proportioned doors at rms 10.8-15.9 px. g003 (1043 px end) agrees: rms 1.2 px at 20.2 vs 8.9 at 20.7. Diagram rejected: it is drawn ~2.5% long.
trace.cab.doors[0]: 377's cab door (0.967-1.787 m) kept as the fit anchor; g018 front edge 2119 px at the top (pick), rear seal 1915-1919 px; g003 1983/1928 px; consistent within the fit. Window: s-cabdoor-018, tall narrow droplight split by a bar at ~40% height (both readers), 377 numbers kept. Body side: train's right (g018, g003); assumed mirrored.
trace.cab.doors[1..2]: g018 row 1436-1471 (bodyside line) projective fit: door 1 leaf edges 1356/1140 px, door 2 537/456 px -> door 1 4.675-6.305 (centre 5.49, width 1.63), door 2 13.985-15.615 (centre 14.80); residuals <=3.4 px (~0.06 m at door 2). Top-row picks give 4.67-6.30/13.99-15.62 (anchors cab door + 20.20 end). g003 top row: 4.67-6.21 / 13.88-15.51 (leaf tops round). The 377's 5.582/14.829 with w 1.76 fits g018 at rms 4.8 px (door-edge residuals +/-8 px) and is rejected; the 1.76 m 377 width likely includes the black surround. Door spacing 9.31 m (377 9.25; dia 9.02 rejected). Door window panes [0.15,0.63] from s-door1-018 (each leaf a tall narrow window roughly central in the leaf; perspective gives 0.04-0.57 and 0.14-0.67 on the two leaves), window rows 1325-1595 px at col 1450 scale -> 1.88-2.85 m. Span kept from the 377.

trace.face.vs377: Every face width here is ~9-13% narrower in metres than classes/377/spec.json (head 0.962 vs 1.06, tail 0.733 vs 0.81, screen outer 1.178 vs 1.336, frame half 0.505 vs 0.597) while the ratios between them match the 377's within 3% (tail/head 0.762 vs 0.764, screen/head 1.22 vs 1.26). The difference is the absolute scale: on g024 the body silhouette sits 73 px (0.24 m) outside the panels; the 377 spec leaves 0.06 m. Heights differ too: the 377's screen bottom 1.875 / lamps 1.37 / panel bottom 1.149 vs 2.062 / 1.655 / 1.436 here; the 379's numbers agree on three photos with independent anchors (g024 width, l017 lamp spacing, g018 rail). The face should be the same Electrostar cab on both classes: the 377 face is worth re-checking against its rail.
trace.liveries.colours: samples.json (each normalised to a white patch in the same light): GN doors = mean(door-018 #313338, door-003 #2C3434); roof = roof-003 #CFCAC7 (roof-018 reflects sky); orange = between orange-024 #FF8833 (clipped red) and orange-l029 #D56223, the bodyside line is too thin to sample (orange-018/003 mix with white); firstStrip = strip-003 #FCE56E (strip-018 #FFE258); yellow = mean(yellow-003 #F0BE2E, yellow-018 #E9B347, yellow-024 #EFA517); gangwayDoor = gwdoor-018; frame = gwframe-018 #5A5555. Window frames near-black (not sampled).
trace.liveries.LE: Sampled separately on l029/l017 (2021): white #EBEAE6 neutral; doors door-l029 #212029 (vs GN #2F3436, both near-black: same paint, gloss/light), first strip strip-l029 #E5B53F (4 px line on a 2021 grazing view, mixes with the orange line), panel yellow yellow-l029 #FFAC1C / yellow-l017 #FEB013, gangway door #FFAB0B (2021 photos are more saturated; GN yellow samples vary #EFA517-#F0BE2E between photos), roof-l029 #7C7B82 is dirt over the cab (not used). Verdict: same paint scheme and the same shapes; only the vinyls differ. LE keeps its own sampled hexes for doors/yellows but they are within the photo-to-photo spread.

trace.cab.faceAhead: 2026-10-05: every cab-car side position moved back 0.20 m from the face and the car lengthened to 20.40 m. Camera matches (375 p814, 379 g018, 387 pkgx/pvic) all fit better with the face further ahead of the doors (fit rms falls for 0.2-0.6 m; 379 g018 passes at 0.2-0.4); the 357 diagram, the only Electrostar nose redrawn rather than copied, puts its face 0.196 m ahead of the 377 drawing's, and the published DM length is 20.39-20.40 m for 357, 377, 379 and 387 alike, so the 377 drawing's 20.20 m face-to-end (from which these positions were carried) is short by the same amount
trace.face.gangwayFrame.bellows: Bellows (the gangway's sides between face and frame): grey rubber, darker and warmer than the pipeline's default #9A9EA2. Sampled on 379 g018 (crop f-gangway-018, the lit side of the folds, x 20-110 y 200-800: median #5E5A51) and balanced against the white bodyside in the same light (white-018 #A7A69F -> #F0F0F0): #87827A. The same Bombardier gangway on every gangwayed Electrostar; measured here.
trace.face.shapes.triangle.radius: A warning triangle's corners are sharp (f-panel crops, g024, l017): rounded 12 mm, not the livery's 60 mm, which turned the 0.19 m triangle into a teardrop (pairs, 2026-10-05).
